Name: collection_policy_coupling_collapse
Title: Rich Get Richer, Twice: The Collection Policy — Not Content Quality — Drives Diversity Collapse When Self-Editing Memory and Prompt Optimization Share the Same Episodes
Short Hypothesis: Degradation in self-evolving agents is caused by the *collection policy*: the episodes that generate new memory items (and new instructions) are themselves executed while conditioned on the current memory, so retrieved items reproduce themselves and the bank's effective support contracts. Content quality is not the lever. Two sharp predictions follow. (1) At matched content volume, growth rate, task draws and write path, a bank grown from memory-OFF episodes preserves retrievable diversity and tail-task accuracy, while the standard coupled loop contracts and accrues a tail-concentrated, break-dominated harm — and content-side write gates (verification/self-consistency) do *not* fix it. (2) Coupling a second self-editing artifact to the same retrieval-conditioned episodes compounds the harm: a reflective prompt optimizer evolved against a contracting bank writes instructions that presuppose the contracted support, so the evolved instruction *transfers* the damage even when paired with a diverse bank. A 50% mixing rate of decoupled collection episodes is the one-line fix.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **The loop as a named object.** CoEvo-Mem (arXiv 2608.01739, 2026) states our exact structural premise — "retrieval determines which memories receive usage signals, while updated memory bank reshape future retrieval" — and treats it as a coupling to *exploit* via joint optimization. This is the strongest adjacency and it is a competing hypothesis, not a scoop: CoEvo-Mem asserts the loop is an efficiency mechanism (usage signals concentrate the bank on what works); we assert it is a preferential-attachment pathology that costs tail coverage. Neither paper runs the arbitrating experiment, which is a decoupled-collection arm at matched content volume. "The Trap of Trajectory" (arXiv 2605.09330) also names the write-back loop, but its causal object is a *content* property (spurious feature–outcome correlations), its measurement is per-item bias, and its remedy is debiasing; it runs no decoupled-collection control and no distributional measurement.

(2) **Degradation attributed to content.** OEP (arXiv 2605.18930) shows locally-correct-but-non-transferable experiences poison the store; "Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget?" (arXiv 2605.09315) documents capability erosion across evolution channels. Both establish the phenomenon and both localize it in what was written, never in what the writes were conditioned on.

(3) **Write-time admission control.** EDV (arXiv 2606.24428), ConsistencyGate (arXiv 2607.22962), Selective Memory Retention (arXiv 2606.29178). These gate content correctness/consistency. Our claim is that a perfectly verified, non-hallucinated, non-spurious item can still be an amplification of what was already retrieved, so these gates should leave the contraction intact. They are our primary competing baseline (arm B2), and a natural stronger competitor is a *diversity*-admission gate (arm B3), which the literature has not separated from correctness gating.

(4) **Diversity collapse elsewhere in the stack.** DecentMem (arXiv 2605.22721) reports diversity collapse in self-evolving multi-agent systems but attributes it to centralized cross-agent sharing; xMemory (arXiv 2602.02007) diagnoses top-k retrieval collapsing "into a single dense region" as a retrieval-side redundancy problem, fixed by hierarchical decoupled retrieval (our read-side alternative, tested implicitly by B1/B3); "Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web" (arXiv 2602.16136) documents dominance/homogenization in RAG caused by *external* synthetic pollution. None isolates a single agent's own read→write coupling.

(5) **Model collapse.** Shumailov et al. (Nature 2024), Alemohammad et al. (Self-Consuming Generative Models Go MAD), SIGMA (arXiv 2601.03385), LLM Web Dynamics (arXiv 2506.15690) supply the formalism — diversity/tail loss under recursive self-generation and fresh-data mixing ratio as the knob — strictly in the weight-training or network-simulation regime. Transplanting it to an append-only text store is not entailed: a memory bank never overwrites the base model, so contraction can act only through retrieval competition, which is exactly why coupled-vs-decoupled collection is the right test.

(6) **Prompt optimization.** MIPRO, GEPA and reflective-evolution successors treat the prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over it. They are normally evaluated against a *static* task distribution. Our second prong asks what happens when the optimizer's own evaluation signal is generated by an agent reading a bank that the optimizer's episodes are simultaneously reshaping — the co-adaptation question the track poses, and one that no prompt-optimization paper we found tests.
Abstract: Self-evolving agents write distillations of their own episodes into a memory bank and retrieve from it on later episodes; a 2026 wave of results shows this degrades performance and attributes the degradation to a property of the written content — hallucinated, spurious, self-confirming, non-transferable — so every proposed remedy is a write-time content filter. We argue the causal variable is the collection policy, not the content. Because episodes are executed while conditioned on retrieved items, the distillations written back are downstream of what was retrieved; retrieval frequency is self-reinforcing and the bank's effective support contracts. We test this with a decoupling design: banks grown over identical cycles from identical task draws with an identical write path and identical write counts, differing only in whether the collecting episodes ran with memory in context. We then make the track's coupling question first-class by crossing that factor with a reflective prompt optimizer, giving a 2×2 over which self-editing channel is coupled to the retrieval-conditioned episodes, and we add an instruction/bank transplant test: if the optimizer's instruction has co-adapted to a contracted support, it should carry the harm to a healthy bank. We measure bank contraction (embedding effective rank, retrieval-count Gini, cluster coverage) against a size-matched random-bank null, and split downstream accuracy into head and tail task clusters with fix/break decompositions. Competing baselines are a correctness-gated write path, a diversity-gated write path, and coupled-but-random retrieval, each of which would win if the mechanism is content quality, coverage-at-write-time, or memory presence per se. A null on coupled-versus-decoupled refutes us and vindicates the content-side account; a coupled arm that beats decoupled on head accuracy with no tail deficit vindicates the "loop as efficiency mechanism" account of CoEvo-Mem. The whole design is one environment, three growth cycles, ~35k episodes on a single 4×A100 node and under $150 of API spend.
Experiments:
HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT: ReAct scaffold, tool stack (a local dense+BM25 Wikipedia retriever), step limit, decoding temperature and seed schedule, the encoder and similarity function used for memory retrieval, the **deployment-time** retrieval protocol (top-k=4, identical in every arm at every evaluation), the write path (identical ExpeL-style distillation prompt and identical success criterion), the training-instance draw sequence, episodes per cycle, and items written per cycle. Arms differ only in how the *collecting* episodes were run and, in the 2×2, whether the instruction is evolved.

ENVIRONMENT (one, deliberately). E1: tool-augmented multi-hop QA over a long-tailed task mixture assembled from HotpotQA (distractor), MuSiQue and 2WikiMultihopQA. Instances are clustered by reasoning template × entity domain into ~20 clusters by embedding k-means plus a frontier-model label on cluster centroids; the training draw distribution is skewed so the five largest clusters cover ~65% of draws. Episodes cost 4–8 model calls. ALFWorld and a second model scale are cut (see changes_made and Risk Factors); long-horizon and cross-scale generality are declared limitations, not claimed.

REGIME (declared, not hidden). Bank starts at 40 items and grows by ≤40 per cycle to ≤160 by cycle 3; deployment k=4. This is a small-bank, high-skew, low-k regime chosen so that contraction, if it exists, is measurable within three cycles. We state this as a design choice and report the measured per-cycle contraction rate so the result can be extrapolated to larger banks rather than asserted for them. The separate "accelerated stress regime" from the previous version is deleted.

MODEL. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the agent throughout. A frontier API model performs offline distillation, prompt-optimizer reflection, and cluster labeling — identically across all arms.

CYCLE PROTOCOL. A shared cycle-0 seed bank is built per seed from 200 memory-off episodes (identical starting point for every arm within a seed). Then three growth cycles. Each cycle: draw 200 training instances (same draw sequence in every arm and seed), run the agent under the arm's collection policy, sample W=40 successful episodes uniformly at random, distill, append. W is capped at the per-seed minimum across arms if any arm cannot produce 40 successes; raw success counts are reported. Bank size trajectories are therefore identical across arms by construction.

ARMS. Core 2×2 (collection policy × instruction policy), 3 seeds each:
- A1 Coupled memory / frozen instruction — the standard self-evolving loop.
- A2 Decoupled memory / frozen instruction — collecting episodes run with NO memory in context; same tasks, same episode count, same write path, same bank size. The core control.
- A3 Coupled memory / co-evolved instruction — GEPA-style reflective optimizer evolves the ReAct system instruction each cycle using failure traces from that cycle's (memory-conditioned) episodes; both self-editing channels coupled.
- A4 Decoupled memory / co-evolved instruction — optimizer evolves against memory-off episodes; bank grown from the same episodes.

Competitors and mechanism ablations, frozen instruction, 2 seeds each:
- B1 Coupled-random-retrieval: collecting episodes still see memory, but items are sampled uniformly from the bank instead of top-k. Separates "similarity-biased retrieval is self-reinforcing" from "any injected memory contracts the bank."
- B2 Content gate (EDV/ConsistencyGate-style): fully coupled, writes must pass verification + self-consistency. If degradation is about content, B2 should track A2.
- B3 Diversity-admission gate: fully coupled, an item is written only if it increases measured bank coverage (marginal gain in effective rank / minimum distance to existing items), independent of correctness. The cheapest competing fix.
- M50 Mixing: 50% of each cycle's collecting episodes run memory-off, 50% coupled. The deployable fix.
- F0 Frozen bank: cycle-0 bank, never grown, evaluated at cycle 3 (evaluation only, no growth cost). Controls for "it is all bank size."

TRANSPLANT TEST (the co-adaptation probe, 3 seeds): evaluate A3's evolved instruction with A4's bank, and A4's evolved instruction with A3's bank. If the harm lives in the bank alone, instruction source should not matter; if the optimizer has co-adapted to a contracted support, A3's instruction should underperform A4's on tail *even on the healthy bank*.

EVALUATION. Frozen held-out test set, n=400, stratified 50/50 head (five largest clusters) / tail, fully paired at the instance level, identical seed schedule for all arms. Evaluations: cycle 0 (shared across arms, once per seed), cycle 2 (A1 and A2 only, trajectory evidence), cycle 3 (all arms + F0 + transplant cells). A no-memory frozen-instruction agent is evaluated once per seed as the common reference for fix/break tables. All results are reported stratum-wise and reweighted to the natural frequency profile. Primary endpoint: cycle-3 tail accuracy, A1 vs A2, paired. Secondary: the 2×2 interaction on tail accuracy (compounding) and the transplant contrast.

BANK-LEVEL CONTRACTION METRICS (no LLM cost; computed every cycle for every arm and seed): (a) effective rank / participation ratio of the item-embedding covariance, under two independent encoders; (b) Gini over per-item retrieval counts accumulated during collection; (c) cluster coverage — distinct clusters represented in top-k retrievals across a fixed 300-query probe set spanning all clusters; (d) redundancy — mean nearest-neighbour similarity among newly written items and novel-n-gram rate versus the cycle-0 bank; (e) size-matched random-bank null: the same metrics for an equal-size bank sampled uniformly from the union of all arms' items, resampled 100×, fixing the value each metric takes under no contraction.

MEDIATION. Mixed-effects model of tail correctness on effective rank and cluster coverage, controlling for bank size and injected token count, pooled over arms/seeds/cycles. The mechanism claim requires that entering contraction metrics substantially attenuates the coupled-arm tail deficit.

COMPUTE ARITHMETIC (the envelope is hard; here is the full accounting).
Collection/training episodes: shared seed banks 3×200 = 600; core arms 4 arms × 3 seeds × 3 cycles × 200 = 7,200; non-core arms 4 × 2 × 3 × 200 = 4,800; prompt-optimizer selection minibatches (A3, A4) 2 arms × 3 seeds × 3 cycles × 6 candidates × 40 instances = 4,320. Subtotal 16,920.
Evaluation episodes: cycle-0 shared 3×400 = 1,200; no-memory reference 3×400 = 1,200; cycle-2 (A1,A2) 2×3×400 = 2,400; cycle-3 core 4×3×400 = 4,800; cycle-3 non-core 4×2×400 = 3,200; F0 3×400 = 1,200; transplant 2 cells ×3×400 = 2,400; null replicates 4 cells ×400 = 1,600. Subtotal 18,000.
Total ≈ 34,900 episodes × ~6 calls = ~210k generations of an 8B model. On 4×A100 with vLLM (4 replicas, 32–64 concurrent episodes, 200–400 output tokens/call) this is ~4–6 GPU-hours of pure generation and ~3–4 days wall clock including local retrieval, orchestration and restarts. Frontier API: 2,520 distillation calls (~7M tokens), 108 optimizer reflection calls on long traces (~1M tokens), cluster labeling (~0.3M tokens) ≈ $120–150 total, inside the few-hundred-dollar budget. Nothing in the design is contingent on spare capacity; there are no optional arms.
Baselines and Ablations:
BASELINES THAT COULD WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.
(i) B2, correctness-gated writes under a fully coupled loop. If verified/self-consistent writes match A2 on tail accuracy and on contraction metrics, the mechanism is content quality and the write-gating literature is right. This is the most likely way the hypothesis dies.
(ii) A1 itself, in the CoEvo-Mem reading: conditioning writes on retrieval concentrates the bank on what actually gets used, an efficiency story rather than a collapse story. Signature: coupled beats decoupled on head accuracy with no tail deficit. We report this as a substantive refutation, not a null.
(iii) B3, diversity-admission gate. If a write-time coverage constraint fully substitutes for decoupling, the cheaper fix wins and "decouple the collection policy" is the wrong recommendation — the mechanism claim survives partially (contraction is the mediator) but the intervention claim does not.
(iv) F0 frozen bank. If a never-grown bank matches everything, the study is about bank size, not the loop.
(v) B1 coupled-random-retrieval. Isolates similarity-biased self-reinforcement from mere memory presence. If B1 contracts as much as A1, the amplification is not retrieval-driven and our account is wrong at the mechanism level even if the phenomenon reproduces.

KEY ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.
A2 is the core control: identical tasks, episode count, write path and bank-size trajectory; self-generated content in both arms; only the feedback removed. The equalized write-count cap removes the differential-success-rate confound (raw counts also reported). The size-matched random-bank null fixes the no-contraction reference for every diversity metric, so declining effective rank cannot be an artifact of bank growth. Head/tail stratification separates "memory gets worse" from "memory gets narrower" — narrowing predicts preserved head, degraded tail, which generic degradation does not. The A3/A4 transplant cells separate contraction stored in the bank from contraction absorbed into the evolved instruction. A shuffled-provenance placebo (item texts relabelled across arms, retrieval unchanged) confirms measured differences track item content rather than bookkeeping. All arms are reported on matched collection-episode, wall-clock and injected-token axes.
Falsifiable Predictions:
If the collection-policy account holds:
1. Bank effective rank in A1 falls ≥30% from cycle 0 to cycle 3 relative to the size-matched random-bank null, while A2 falls <10%, with direction consistent across all 3 seeds and both encoders.
2. Retrieval-count Gini in A1 exceeds 0.6 by cycle 3 and top-k cluster coverage over the probe set drops ≥25%, while A2 stays flat (within the random-bank null band).
3. The downstream signature is asymmetric: at cycle 3, A1 tail accuracy is ≥6 points below A2 (paired, clears the stated MDE), while head accuracy differs by <4 points in either direction (equivalence margin, see Measurement). The harm shows up as a rising *break* count against the no-memory reference on tail instances, not merely as missing fixes.
4. Content gating does not rescue: B2's cycle-3 tail accuracy is within 3 points of A1 and its effective-rank decline is within 10 percentage points of A1's, i.e. B2 tracks A1 and not A2. B1 (random retrieval under a coupled loop) contracts substantially less than A1 (≥half the A1→A2 gap recovered), showing the amplification is retrieval-similarity-driven.
5. Mixing works with a visible, non-linear benefit: M50 recovers ≥two-thirds of the A1→A2 tail gap.
6. **Compounding (the coupling claim).** A3 (both channels coupled) has the lowest tail accuracy of the 2×2, and the negative interaction term exceeds 8 points — the honest MDE for a 2×2 interaction at our n. If the interaction is smaller than that, we report the main effects and explicitly declare the compounding claim underpowered rather than asserting it.
7. **Transplant.** A3's evolved instruction, paired with A4's diverse bank, loses ≥4 points of tail accuracy relative to A4's instruction on the same bank. This is the sharp form of co-adaptation: the instruction, not just the bank, carries the contraction.
8. Mediation: entering effective rank and cluster coverage attenuates the coupled-arm tail deficit by ≥half.

REFUTATION CONDITIONS. If A1 and A2 are indistinguishable at cycle 3 on both contraction metrics and tail accuracy, the coupling account is dead, self-generated content per se is what matters, and we report that as the primary result in support of the write-gating literature. If B2 matches A2 on all endpoints, the mechanism is content quality and our framing is wrong. If A1 beats A2 on head with no tail deficit, the loop is an efficiency mechanism (CoEvo-Mem's premise) and we say so. If B3 matches A2, the correct fix is diversity-aware writing, not decoupled collection. If contraction metrics move exactly as predicted but tail accuracy does not follow, the bank narrows without measurable downstream cost at this horizon — a real but much weaker finding, and we pre-commit to reporting it as such. If the transplant contrast is null while the bank contrast holds, contraction lives entirely in the bank and the optimizer is an innocent bystander.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Three variance sources, handled separately.

(a) EVALUATION VARIANCE. Every arm at every cycle is evaluated on the same held-out instances with the same seed schedule, so all arm comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar on paired fix/break tables, Holm-corrected across the arm family within each cycle and stratum; every delta is reported with its fix/break decomposition, because a flat net accuracy hiding growing symmetric churn is a distinct finding.

(b) BANK-TRAJECTORY VARIANCE, the source specific to this study. Core arms (A1–A4) are grown three independent times with the same training-instance draw sequence and different decoding seeds; non-core arms twice. Arm effects come from a mixed-effects logistic model with crossed random intercepts for test instance and bank trajectory; CIs from a cluster bootstrap resampling trajectories as well as instances. Because cycle 0 is by construction identical across arms, the cycle-3 arm contrast *is* a difference-in-differences and any constant trajectory offset cancels.

(c) NULL REPLICATES. Four arm-cycle cells (A1 and A2 at cycle 3, two extra decoding seeds each) are re-run with no treatment change; the distribution of apparent deltas gives the empirical noise floor. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. This is load-bearing given prior observations of 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment. Contraction metrics have their own null: the size-matched random bank, resampled 100× per cycle.

MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECTS, and what we therefore do not claim. With 200 paired tail instances per arm-cycle-seed and an expected 12–18% discordant-pair rate, a single cell detects ≈7 points at 80% power. Pooling 3 trajectories in the mixed model, with a between-trajectory SD of 2–3 points estimated from the null replicates, the A1-vs-A2 tail contrast is detectable at ≈5–6 points; prediction 3 is stated at 6. The head stratum at the same n cannot certify equivalence tighter than ≈4 points, so "head unaffected" is an equivalence claim at a 4-point margin and anything inside that band is reported as inconclusive. The 2×2 interaction has roughly twice the standard error of a main effect, giving an MDE of ≈8–10 points; prediction 6 is stated at 8 and we pre-commit to declaring it underpowered otherwise rather than reporting a suggestive interaction as support. The transplant contrast (3 seeds, 400 paired instances, same-bank comparison) supports a ≈4-point MDE on tail. Non-core arms at 2 seeds support only ≈7–8 point contrasts and their predictions (4, 5) are stated at that resolution. The 50/50 head/tail stratification is deliberate: the natural tail frequency would leave the decisive slice underpowered; all frequency-weighted numbers are reported as reweighted estimates with their own bootstrap intervals.
Preprint Collision Check:
The literature search run for this revision returned one work that is a direct mechanistic adjacency and several partial ones.

**Closest: CoEvo-Mem (arXiv 2608.01739, 2026).** It names our exact structural loop — "retrieval determines which memories receive usage signals, while updated memory bank reshape future retrieval" — and calls it a fundamental feedback loop that prior methods overlook. This is the strongest threat and I will not minimize it: the mechanistic premise is essentially identical. It does not collide on the *claim*, because CoEvo-Mem treats the loop as a resource to co-optimize and predicts it helps; we predict it is a preferential-attachment pathology whose cost is tail coverage. Neither their paper nor any other runs the arbitrating experiment — a decoupled-collection arm at matched content volume, growth rate and write path — and CoEvo-Mem reports no bank-level diversity measurement and no head/tail decomposition. Our design is set up so that CoEvo-Mem's premise is a live outcome (baseline (ii)): if coupled beats decoupled on head with no tail deficit, they are right and we say so. That said, a reviewer is entitled to read our contribution as "testing CoEvo-Mem's premise adversarially," and that is a fair characterization of prong 1.

**Partial collisions.** "The Trap of Trajectory" (arXiv 2605.09330) names the write-back loop but localizes causation in a content property (spurious correlations), measures per-item bias, and fixes it by debiasing; no decoupled control, no distributional measurement. DecentMem (arXiv 2605.22721) reports diversity collapse in self-evolving multi-agent systems but attributes it to centralized cross-agent memory sharing, a different cause with a different fix. xMemory (arXiv 2602.02007) diagnoses top-k retrieval "collapsing into a single dense region" as a static retrieval-side redundancy problem; this is the read-side alternative explanation our B1/B3 arms are designed to separate from write-side coupling. "Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web" (arXiv 2602.16136, WWW 2026) documents dominance/homogenization in RAG but from external synthetic pollution, not an internal loop. OEP (2605.18930), "Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget?" (2605.09315), EDV (2606.24428) and ConsistencyGate (2607.22962) are content-quality accounts and content-side gates; the latter two are implemented as arm B2. ReasoningBank (2509.25140) and the 2026 memory surveys (2602.06052, 2603.07670) presume the loop is benign; 2603.07670 notes that observability into which items are retrieved versus written-but-never-read is "almost entirely absent in agent memory practice," which is an engineering observation adjacent to our Gini/coverage instrumentation but not a collapse claim.

**Gap that survives the search.** No retrieved work isolates the collection policy — whether the collecting episodes were conditioned on retrieval — as the causal variable, none frames the dynamic as preferential attachment with a measurable contraction rate against a size-matched null, and none crosses it with prompt optimization or runs an instruction/bank transplant. The prompt-optimization prong appears unaddressed entirely: I found no work testing what a reflective optimizer does when its own evaluation episodes are reshaping the memory it is optimizing against.

**Honest caveat.** I could not sweep OpenReview 2026 submissions, and a memory-off collection ablation could plausibly appear in an appendix of a sibling preprint. If CoEvo-Mem's camera-ready contains a decoupled-collection ablation, prong 1 becomes a replication-plus-mediation result and prong 2 (compounding and transplant) carries the contribution.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Three cycles may be too short.** We deleted the separate accelerated stress regime and instead chose a primary regime (40-item seed bank, ≤160 items, k=4, strongly skewed draws) in which contraction is plausibly measurable within three cycles. This is declared, not hidden, and it bounds generality: a null at cycle 3 is evidence about this regime, and we report the measured per-cycle contraction rate so readers can extrapolate rather than assume.
2. **Single environment, single model scale.** ALFWorld and the 14B replication are cut for the compute envelope. Long-horizon and cross-scale generality are stated as limitations; the paper claims a mechanism in an 8B-class tool-QA agent, not a universal law. We would rather run one adequately powered environment than two underpowered ones.
3. **Differential success rates** change how many items each arm would write; we equalize by capping at the per-seed minimum and subsampling uniformly, which departs slightly from pure deployment practice. Both equalized and raw-count trajectories are reported.
4. **Head/tail clusters are defined by us**, and a bad definition could manufacture the asymmetry. Clusters are fixed in advance from the training pool by automatic embedding clustering plus a frontier-model label on centroids, frozen before any evaluation, with taxonomy and cluster sizes published and a human check of 150 assignments reported with kappa.
5. **Diversity metrics are encoder-dependent**; effective rank is reported under two independent encoders, and the size-matched random-bank null — not the absolute value — is the reference.
6. **The compounding claim is the least powered part of the design.** A 2×2 interaction at our n needs ~8 points to be certified; we pre-commit to reporting an unresolved interaction as unresolved. The transplant test is the better-powered route to the same co-adaptation claim, which is why it was added.
7. **Contraction without downstream cost** is a plausible outcome and much weaker; we pre-commit to reporting it as "the bank narrows without measurable cost at this horizon."
8. **The prompt optimizer is one specific reflective/evolutionary instantiation** (GEPA-style instruction evolution, 6 candidates/cycle, 40-instance selection minibatches). A different optimizer with a larger search budget might co-adapt differently; the optimizer budget is held identical across A3 and A4 so the *contrast* is clean even if the absolute optimizer strength is modest.
